0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Touraine is known for its reds and Vouvray, but its white-wine map is far richer than you might think. Five distinctive white (and a little rosé) AOCs — from Cheverny beside its château, to Cour-Cheverny, which permits a single near-extinct variety, to the ancient Valençay — make up the four corners of Touraine whites and take you through the most overlooked facets of the land of châteaux.

Learning Objectives

🌿 Get to know Romorantin — one of the world's rarest varieties

Cour-Cheverny AOC is the only AOC in the world that permits Romorantin, a variety that survives almost only on a few dozen hectares (around 50 ha) in Cour-Cheverny

🏰 Grasp the logic of Cheverny's multi-variety blends

How a Sauvignon Blanc-led blend with Chardonnay, Chenin and others shows distinctive character on the gravel-sand soils near the château

🗺️ Learn Valençay's location and varietal features

How Valençay, close to the Berry, links the wine worlds of Touraine and the central vineyards
1.title: Cheverny AOC — Elegant Blended Whites Beside the Château
1.highlights.0.content: Cheverny AOC takes the famous Château de Cheverny (the model for Moulinsart Castle in The Adventures of Tintin) as its landmark, with vineyards spread around the château
1.highlights.1.title: Blending rules
1.highlights.1.content: White: Sauvignon (including Sauvignon Gris) 60–84%, Chardonnay, Chenin, Orbois and others 16–40%. This blending gives Cheverny a rounder texture than pure Sauvignon Blanc
1.highlights.2.title: Gravel-sand soils
1.highlights.2.content: The sandy gravel soils of the Touraine plain drain extremely well, making fresh, light whites with pure fruit and moderate acidity, best drunk young at 1–4 years
1.content:
Cheverny AOC (recognised in 1993, covering red, white and rosé) has as its most important feature the blending logic of its whites: Sauvignon Blanc leads, but the addition of Chardonnay and other varieties (16–40% in total) brings a rounder texture and fuller body, setting it apart from the pure Sauvignon Blanc style (such as Sancerre).

Reds are mainly Pinot Noir (60–84%) with Gamay as support (16–40%), with small amounts of Cabernet Franc and Côt also permitted; the style is light and an excellent weeknight table wine. Overall, Cheverny is one of Touraine's best-value fine AOCs, with an average price of €12–20.

Representative estates: Domaine du Salvard (organic farming, Cheverny's best-known fine estate), Domaine Tesier
2.title: Cour-Cheverny AOC — Romorantin's Last Refuge
2.content:
Cour-Cheverny AOC is an extremely special case: it is the only AOC in the world that permits growing and making wine from the Romorantin variety, which has almost vanished from France's wine map and survives stubbornly only on a few dozen hectares in Cour-Cheverny.

🌿 Romorantin variety profile

Historical origins

DNA research shows Romorantin is an offspring of Pinot and Gouais Blanc (an ancient, almost extinct variety), related to Chardonnay. The name comes from the small town of Romorantin-Lanthenay in the Loir-et-Cher department, and King Francis I is said to have introduced it there in the 16th century.

Viticultural traits

Late ripening, high acidity and disease-prone — precisely these "flaws" led farmers to replant to other varieties on a large scale in the 20th century, so that Romorantin can almost only keep producing in Cour-Cheverny's special gravel-sand soils and microclimate.

Style characteristics

Extremely high acidity, low to medium body, and a distinctive aroma of honey + flint minerality + acacia blossom. Extremely closed when young, sometimes even too sharp, but after 5–10 years of ageing it shows astonishing complexity and mineral depth.

Cour-Cheverny is one of France's hardest AOCs to understand, but also one most worth waiting patiently for. If you can get a bottle of Cour-Cheverny Romorantin from Domaine du Salvard or Domaine des Huards, put it in the cellar and open it after 8 years — it will be an unforgettable experience. Average price €15–35.
3.title: Valençay & Touraine Village Whites
3.content:
🧀 Valençay AOC (recognised in 2004)

Location: Indre department, beside the Château de Valençay (also the home of the famous cheese!), close to the Berry, the southeasternmost region of Touraine

White varieties: Sauvignon Blanc (main, usually 70–80%) + Arbois (Menu Pineau, adding more herbal spice)

Style: crisp, herbal, white-floral, softer than Sancerre and with more character than Touraine Sauvignon, average price €10–18

Of interest: Valençay cheese (a goat cheese) and Valençay white wine are both products of the same AOC area, one of France's most perfect "one place, one food, one wine" pairings

🏰 Touraine-Amboise Blanc

Variety: Chenin Blanc (main), the white wine of the area beside the Château d'Amboise

Style: crisper and lighter than Vouvray, suited to drinking young, with dishes of the château area (freshwater fish, white meat)

🌸 Touraine-Azay-le-Rideau Blanc

Variety: Chenin Blanc (the only one permitted), in the small valley of the Indre beside the Château d'Azay-le-Rideau

Style: dry or slightly sweet (Demi-Sec), with fresh white-flower and apple aromas, one of Touraine's most romantic whites — suited to a lunch in the château gardens
4.title: Quick Quiz
4.questions.0.question: What is the greatest distinction of Cour-Cheverny AOC?
4.questions.0.options.0: It is Touraine's largest white-wine AOC
4.questions.0.options.1: It is the only AOC in the world that permits wine made from Romorantin
4.questions.0.options.3: It is Touraine's only Grand Cru-level region
4.questions.0.explanation: Cour-Cheverny AOC is the world's only appellation that permits the Romorantin variety (100%), a near-extinct variety that survives only on a few dozen hectares in Cour-Cheverny, showing a distinctive style of high acidity and flint minerality.
4.questions.1.question: How does the blending of Cheverny AOC whites set them apart from the pure Sauvignon Blanc style?
4.questions.1.options.0: Because of the honey sweetness of added Chenin Blanc
4.questions.1.options.1: The addition of Chardonnay and other varieties (16–40% in total) brings a rounder texture and fuller body, making it rounder than pure Sauvignon Blanc
4.questions.1.options.2: Because of long ageing in plenty of new oak barrels
4.questions.1.options.3: Because Cabernet Franc is blended in, adding complexity
4.questions.1.explanation: What makes Cheverny whites distinctive is the blend of Sauvignon (60–84%) + Chardonnay/Chenin/Orbois (16–40%) — Chardonnay and the others bring a rounded body, giving Cheverny more layers and fullness than the pure Sauvignon Blanc style (such as Sancerre).
